problem: "Every element generates a rectangular box" is too absolute: an element with display: none generates no box at all, and a non-replaced inline element generates line boxes where vertical padding and borders paint without changing line height. A student reading this literally will be confused by display: none later.
fix: "Every element that the browser draws generates a rectangular box (display: none generates none). From the outside in, the box has four layers: margin, border, padding and content."

problem: "Only margins accept negative values" is over-broad and reads as a rule about all of CSS, not about the box model. Properties outside the box model (text-indent, letter-spacing, top/left on positioned boxes, transform) do take negative values.
fix: "Of the four box-model spacing properties, only margin accepts negative values; padding and border-width cannot be negative."

problem: The border-box explanation and the content-width formula cover width only. Students then apply the same subtraction wrongly to height, or do not know it behaves the same way.
fix: Add one sentence: "The same arithmetic applies to height: content height = declared height − top/bottom padding − top/bottom border." Also note that if padding and border exceed the declared size, the content box shrinks to 0, not below.

problem: Two small points that exam answers often need are missing: percentage margins and padding are resolved against the width of the containing block (even for top and bottom), and margin: auto on the vertical axis computes to 0 for block boxes in normal flow.
fix: Add: "A percentage margin or padding is calculated from the width of the containing block, including padding-top and padding-bottom. Vertically, auto margins on a block box evaluate to 0 unless a layout mode such as flex or grid is in use."

problem: "display decides how a box treats width and vertical margins" is vague and slightly misleading; display decides what kind of box is generated (block-level, inline-level, or none), which then decides how width and vertical margins apply.
fix: "display decides what kind of box the element generates. A block-level box starts on a new line and respects width, height and all margins; an inline box sits in a line of text, where width, height and vertical margins do not apply."
